notes.title: Update 1.4
notes.content:
Hello,

Our final major update for ViruaCreature has arrived! We really wanted to make sure the game was in a good state, and had potential to grow even without content support from us in the future. So, as of this update VirtuaCreature has been fully open-sourced; both the game code and the previously released server code can be modified by players to enhance or alter their experience as much as desired. More information on this is available below.

Patch Notes

 Mods can now be loaded over the base game; ModLoader launch option added to configure
 Included "Legacy Mode" mod to play enhanced 2020 Legacy Version
 The 4 postgame boss creatures can now be obtained via evolution at level 75
 Boss creatures now have an ability
 Buffed stats for all boss creatures
 Clearing a Boss Tower that ends with a boss creature now nets a reward drop; scales by difficulty and includes XP Boosts
 All level/mod points add 2 points to the relevant stat instead of 1
 Updated movesets for all Challenger creatures to include moves previously locked to Champions
 The move shop is now locked until you've reached the relevant tutorial
 Reworked offline mode screens to be more informative and link to server hosting
 Reworked Creature Wiki screens to be cleaner and include boss creatures
 Updated text on Rebirth screen to match current implementation
 Fixed Rebirth not increasing the level cap
 Fixed incorrect Void Mine drops
 Fixed tutorial arrows incorrectly spawning on stat, info & cooking screens
 Fixed some tutorials resetting after Rebirth
 Fixed Full Arsenal achievement not being triggered
 Fixed Genus being oversized on some screens


Creating or using Mods
If you're interested in creating mods for VirtuaCreature, the client code can be found on our Github. Please note that compiling your mod requires some proprietary Adobe software as explained in the repo's Readme.

If you're interested in playing a mod, you will have to look around. Steam Workshop support is not currently implemented, and probably won't be unless a community around mods pops up; instead, we'd recommend you check the game's discussion board, or join our Discord!

If you've found a mod to play, simply move the provided mods folder to your installation directory, and select "Configure ModLoader" as your launch option in Steam. You'll then be presented with a list you can select and boot.

We hope you have fun with this new update, and with VirtuaCreature for many years to come!

notes.title: Important update on servers
notes.content:
Hello,

After careful consideration, we've decided it's no longer in our best interest to continue running the VirtuaCreature servers. It is quite expensive, we don't bring in the required revenue to break even and we currently don't have any projects coming up using the same infrastructure. So, the servers will officially cease all operations April 7, 2024.

However, this is not cause for alarm! We strongly believe in preserving online games after they're gone, and to do our part we've decided to undertake the following actions:


 The server code has been adapted into a publicly available repository, so anyone can host their own servers and play online! This is fully identical to the master server aside from the authentication and old monetization code, which has been stripped.
 VirtuaCreature will receive an update on the day of shutdown that switches the game into automatic offline mode, so all singleplayer content can be effortlessly accessed from this point forward. This will also enable connection to any unofficial server by moving a single configuration file into the installation directory.


If you're interested in hosting a server for yourself or the public, the repo is available now. Please note that it is not exactly beginner friendly and we aren't offering any extended support on server hosting at this time. Game clients will not be able to connect to any unofficial server until the update is live - this is just to get a headstart on the hosting process.

We hope this solution can create the best experience for our players! There is more on the horizon as well, so don't count us out just yet.

notes.title: Pricing changes & the future of VirtuaCreature
notes.content:
Hello,

We have some big changes to announce for how players will engage with VirtuaCreature, as well as updates to the game itself.

Monetization Model
We tried our best to present a Free-To-Play model that was both fair and engaging for our playerbase, first with a more typical mtx-based model, and later completely replacing it with a single, simple DLC to unlock all features. Despite our efforts, this simply didn't pan out. Even now, long after the dust has settled, Legacy Version regularly outperforms this current version of the game in sales - a much older build of the game with less content, little to no tutorialization and a worse engine holding the core of the experience back. What this clearly signals to us is that you guys, the playerbase, would much rather pay once and be done with it than deal with any type of F2P system, simple or not.

Frankly, we agree! So, that has guided our decision to convert VirtuaCreature to a regular paid product like most others on Steam. There are a number of key changes accopanying this conversion:


 The Premium Upgrade will be delisted and will no longer be purchasable.
 Any in-game features that were locked or limited by the Premium Upgrade will now be fully available to all players. This includes all storage boxes for creatures, inventory slots, the standard XP rate etc.
 Cosmetic perks, aka the borders and profile icons, will now be mostly available to all players - more details on this below.


Players who have already added the game to their account while it was free will get to keep it and will be receiving the above changes as well.

If you have already purchased the Premium Upgrade, or purchase it before this transition, you will be privy to a few exclusive perks:


 7 XP Boosts, lasting 24 Hours each, will be available to redeem at any time. These will refresh on starting a new game as well.
 The "Ukiyoe" border, which will not be available to regular players, will be unlocked.
 A new "Statue" profile icon, which will not be available to regular players, will be unlocked.


We hope these changes will create the best possible experience for our players going forward.

Game Update
A regular update will also be pushed alongside these changes, mainly consisting of backend changes we've been building up over the last few months. However, there are some noticeable new things as well:


 The game will now use 64bit builds instead of 32bit. This will not affect the vast majority of the playerbase, however if by some slim chance you are running a 32bit OS, your system will no longer be supported.
 Rich Presence for Steam! Your friends can now see exactly what you're getting up to, or if there's space to join your multiplayer match.
 A small collection of fixes, including some user-reported issues.


We'd be interested in doing more "auxiliary" updates like this in the future, though that all depends on how smoothly this transition goes. We'll keep you posted!

Legacy Version merge
We will be delisting the "Legacy Version" of VirtuaCreature from sale. If you're still interested in playing this older version of the game, we have merged it into this version! Simply go to the beta tab in the game's properties and select the "legacy" branch and the game will update accordingly.

If you have any questions about these upcoming changes, please feel free to leave a comment here, on our discord or in the forums and we'll get back to you.

Happy playing!

Hello,

I come to you today with a breakdown of our new event system, and an update for the future of the game:

Monthly Campaigns
Starting today, there will be a new set of challenges that will be generated on the first day of the month and run until the last, every month into the future. Think of these like daily missions, but with higher task requirements (and higher rewards!). You can find these on the same screen as the daily missions by hitting the page turn button.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38556718/6fd520b77fcacb0113a94fe959b72264e36bbebc.png

You can also find this in the news section of the Network Hub, which will display the end date:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38556718/63cf69a506ffd659b84fc76e4a67a694536bf9fa.png

Development Update
With the completion of the 1.3.x patches and our server update, we've officially reached the end of planned development for VirtuaCreature, and will be transitioning into "maintenance mode". If we find any important bugs, we will fix and deploy them, and we might even run some events here and there, but this marks the end of new features or major changes. Online features will remain operational, and we plan to keep it that way for a long time.

Given the age of the game's core, we feel we've pushed VirtuaCreature as far as we can within its reasonable limits, and are ready to move on and pursue new projects. We're very thankful for anyone who stops in sometimes to play, and hope many more of you will come explore what we've built over years to come.

Thank you for reading!

notes.title: Important changes coming to VirtuaCreature
notes.content:
Hello,

Thank you to all our players for supporting VirtuaCreature. We have some major changes coming soon, so we'd like to clearly outline them here in advance.

Business model overhaul
We are no longer interested in running a F2P economy, as it has not only been unsuccessful but feels increasingly cruel trying to design. As such, all microtransaction elements are being removed; this includes the Gold Synths that were directly purchasable, as well as all items from the Premium Shop.

In their place will be a single, permanent purchase called the Premium Upgrade. Here is what your purchase will unlock:


 A permanent 2x XP boost for all creatures
 All 6 Creature Boxes available
 1024 slots for Chest, Equipment & Cooking storage
 12 Cosmetic Borders
 12 Profile Icons

While all purchasing options for individual items will no longer be available, some in-game methods of obtaining said items will persist. These include:


 Revives can be obtained through Daily Missions, events or playing multiplayer matches
 Temporary XP Boosts can be obtained through Daily Missions, events or playing multiplayer matches
 Profile Icons not unlocked by the Premium Upgrade can be obtained through events or playing multiplayer matches

Additionally, a few mechanics will either be altered or removed:


 The default amount of Creature Boxes available to all players will be 1 instead of 2
 Account Renaming will no longer be available

Finally, it should be noted that previous purchases will not transfer over. Any purchased Gold Synths or items obtained with them will no longer be available after this update.

How to purchase the new Premium Upgrade
The Premium Upgrade will be available as a DLC on the game's store page. Players can also be directed to said DLC landing page via relevant in-game buttons.

We hope these changes will lead to a better, more stable player experience going forward.

Account wipe
Due to both the huge overhaul of our monetization as well as various security & structural flaws with our current account system, we've decided to reset our servers and wipe all user accounts. Players who open the game after the next update will be prompted to create a new account, or back out of the process entirely and play with online features restricted. To be clear, the data for current accounts will not be maintained or held by us, and likewise will not be accessible to any players.

Please note that this will not effect your save data! Your in-game progress and creatures will not be altered after this update, only data directly related to your account, such as purchases, Player Level, quantity of Revives & XP Boosts, etc.


If you have any questions or concerns regarding this information, please reach out to us or leave a comment in relevant spaces and we'd be happy to address it. This update & overhaul is planned to release in May, however if we find any critical issues we will resolve them before moving forward with a release.

This is a version of the announcement edited specifically for Steam users. If you'd like to see how these changes will effect all platforms, you can do so here.

Development Update
We've kept quiet since late 2021, as we've been deciding what exactly we want the long-term future for this game to be. While there is a fairly clear plan in place now, it has not progressed far enough that I want to openly come forward with details; this will most likely have to wait until a bit further into the year.

In short, we're planning on revamping VirtuaCreature's ecosystem to make it more fair and simple for players. This will coincide with a consolidation of our servers, which will help keep our running costs low. Our hope is that these things can keep the game alive for the foreseeable future, as we would like to continue running it even if it isn't our main priority. We hope you'll stick around to see!

See you all soon!

notes.title: VirtuaForecast - May
notes.content:
Hello,

We hope you've all been enjoying VC so far! In an effort to be transparent, I've decided to put together this news segment going over the current status of development and how things are going. I may do these in the future as well, if need be. So, without further ado, let's get into it.

Launch Progress
Let's get the negativity out of the way. To be completely blunt: We have failed our launch goal. While we did kick off with a decent amount of momentum, player numbers quickly dropped off, and our returning player rate has been very low. Multiplayer is DOA, which is disappointing because we thought it would be a good source for content generation & events, particularly the co-op. In fact, we have yet to even make a single dollar in revenue.

All I can really ask for is that people support the game monetarily if they enjoy it. We have a variety of purchasable items, including some cool cosmetics like border art. As of now, the future of the game is uncertain, as the idea of running this continually at a loss in the hope it'll improve is not too appealing.

Of course, this isn't really the fault of the playerbase at all. Based on feedback from public reviews and some firsthand talks with people, the number one thing we heard was lack of clarity from within the game. It's a lot to learn at the start, with multiple important mechanics mostly left up to discovery, and players get confused and walk away before putting any significant time in. So, what are we doing about it?

Improved Tutorials
This is the biggest thing we've been working on since launch, and hopefully it shows. For the sake of simplicity, I'll break this into two categories: Explicit Tutorialization, where the game is deliberately telling you something, versus Implicit Tutorialization, where it is simply suggesting it. Both of these elements are currently lacking, as trial & error is the only way to learn most of the inner systems. There is an element of mystery to this that can be enjoyable, but having it applied universally is unappealing and esoteric to most people.

Our immediate counter to a lack of explicit tutorials was to fill the game with text boxes, of both mandatory & optional varieties, that explain things in detail. While giving players in-depth options to learn about your game is never a bad thing, for a casual game like this text isn't really appropriate as the sole method for doing so, and the numbers reflect that. To rectify this, we're introducing tutorial arrows to help guide new players.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38556718/f86a039b1c6d9a1dc429538d4d1731fa1a7c1ff3.gif

After the majority of the mandatory textboxes, an arrow (or set of arrows for more complicated actions) will guide players through their first interactions with the explained system. Other buttons will be locked until this is completed. Hopefully, this will ensure no new player is left behind when it comes to the basic mechanics.

For implicit tutorials, we're making an effort to go over various parts of the game and trying to clean up our visual language. For example, on the recipes screen, right now all recipe icons are plainly displayed, and whether or not they're unlocked will only display after hovering over or selecting said icon, in text. This has been changed to display a "?" on the icon when the recipe is undiscovered.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38556718/007e87e78ad3c1f5aeeb517b9f7b92615be7c03e.png

Similarly, another user expressed frustration in figuring out which moves could be learned by each creature, so we've added an incompatibility display on the move shop.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38556718/c82d54909557630b1b8f7bea7773bf01a80e52f9.png

With better, more consistent information displays, users should be able to grasp more complex ideas without resorting to outside help or tedious experimentation.

Arena & Tower Reworks
As our most important mechanics, the presentation for our various combat modes should be kept consistent with each other. Currently, they're not at all, with entirely different UI between the Arena, Tower & Multiplayer modes.

For those who don't know, this game has been in development for a very long time. There is a previous iteration from 2018-2021 available on Steam (with initial development started 2 years before even that), and this is built on an improved version of that foundation, with most of the visuals carried over. Over that large gap, our design philosophy has improved a lot, and many of the old areas of the game were left in the dust; classic scope creep. To help bring everything closer together, we've completely replaced the Arena/Tower menus, to now be under one unified design!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38556718/41070b958097b107d28ea064115dfa5e09046cb5.gif

Content types are now sorted categorically instead of all under a single list, and locked content will display visually instead of requiring the user to select and be denied entry. Rather than plain text buttons spread across the screen to select difficulty, the difficulty slider from the co-op mode has been brought over. For modes without difficulty options (i.e. Infinite, Max, Impossible variants) there are now short descriptions in its place for those who don't know what they are yet!

Additionally, the unlock text that displays after clearing a tower has been overhauled, both for more detailed information and extra functionality. It will now specify whether you unlocked a new difficulty, a new menu selection, or multiple menu selections; this now also applies to the arenas, which are unlocked based on level rather than linear progression.

Finally, this new modular take on the menus allows for expansion much easier than before, which is the last thing we plan on adding before this update rolls out; no promises yet, but we're looking to significantly increase the singleplayer content available in the endgame.

Next Steps
The plan is to get this update out by mid-June at the latest, if not earlier, depending on how fast the new content can be balanced. We've paused any advertising or growth efforts in the meantime, as it seems like a waste while the player turnover rate is so high. If anyone has been sticking with us, we very much appreciate you, and hope you'll stay around for a long time if possible.

If we can course correct this game's trajectory, we have a fun event schedule that was being worked out, new content ideas, and lots of additional improvements to make. If we can't, however, I personally can't imagine the game can go on in this form that much longer. We're dedicated to preserving it no matter the outcome, but some drastic changes will have to be implemented in a worst case scenario.

We're doing our best, and we'll see you all soon!

We recommend linking to ensure you can share everything possible between your devices!

Feedback & Bug Reports
If you have early feedback or bugs to report, we have a thread for that! We will also be answering any early questions. Pop in and give us your thoughts!

Launch / Bug Report Thread

Follow Us
Finally, if you'd like to easily keep up with us, follow us on social media!

 Instagram


We hope you have fun playing VirtuaCreature!

Additionally, we would appreciate it if any interested players wishlisted us on Steam and followed our social media to stay in touch with news regarding the full release. We look forward to welcoming more of you in Q1 2021 on Steam, iOS & Android platforms!

See you all again soon!

notes.title: VirtuaCreature Autumn Demo
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We're going to be participating in the Steam Autumn Game Festival! We're super excited to show off our progress in such a big way, and do we ever have stuff to show! Starting October 7th, you'll be able to try out both single and multiplayer content for VirtuaCreature for a limited time!

What content will be playable during the demo period?

Try a sampling of single-player content including battling, minigames, crafting, character customization and more!
Raise up to 6 creatures! Experiment and grow each one differently to see the many possible evolutions and builds.
Go online and test your mettle against real-life opponents! Both public and private modes are available, so bring your friends or queue up for random matches!


How will this demo compare to the final release?

The demo has a much faster XP curve to allow players to quickly access content without grinding.
Online play is currently missing many features; the release version will contain a proper account system, more diverse rewards for matches, timed events, cosmetic customization and a planned co-op mode.
Some elements of the single-player experience are lacking planned features, and many areas lack polish or proper tutorialization; feel free to ask us questions on the forums!
The release version will feature a F2P economy.
The demo does not contain any Steamworks features such as Cloud Saves or Achievements; this is planned for release.
Some late game single-player content has been locked or hidden to help prevent spoilers.


Have fun, and we hope to see you all again soon!
